questions.question: A "thoracic aortic aneurysm" (TAA) is generally defined when the diameter of the ascending aorta exceeds:
questions.detail: Diameters greater than 4 cm in the ascending aorta are generally considered aneurysmal.

questions.question: In a patient with Marfan syndrome, the "tulip bulb" appearance of the aortic root is a manifestation of:
questions.detail: This features dilation of the sinuses of Valsalva and the aortic annulus, which is characteristic of collagen vascular diseases.

questions.question: Which vasculitis characteristically affects the aortic arch and its primary branches in young women, leading to stenosis or occlusion?
questions.detail: Also known as "pulseless disease," Takayasu Arteritis causes granulomatous inflammation of the large vessels in young patients.

questions.question: "Giant Cell Arteritis" (GCA) typically involves which of the following vessels?
questions.detail: GCA is a large vessel vasculitis seen in older adults and is often associated with Polymyalgia Rheumatica.

questions.question: On a chest radiograph, the "figure-3 sign" and "rib notching" are classic indicators of:
questions.detail: The "3" is formed by pre- and post-stenotic dilation, while rib notching results from collateral flow through intercostal arteries.

questions.question: "Post-ductal" coarctation is the most common type in adults and is located:
choices: Distal to the left subclavian artery origin
questions.detail: This is the adult (post-ductal) type of coarctation, which often remains asymptomatic until later in life.

questions.question: "Pseudocoarctation" differs from true coarctation because it:
choices: Lacks a pressure gradient or collateral circulation
questions.detail: Pseudocoarctation is an anatomical "kinking" of the aorta that lacks hemodynamically significant narrowing.

questions.question: A "shaggy" or "cobblestone" appearance of the aortic wall on angiography is a sign of:
questions.detail: This irregular contour of the aortic wall is a marker of high-risk atherosclerotic plaque.
